messages:
maya: Thanks everyone for the runtime deep dive — a few follow-ups from the All-Hands.
maya: First: KV cache eviction. Are we going to support per-tenant TTLs or only global eviction heuristics? Thinking about regulated customers who want max-residency guarantees.
taylor: Good question. Short answer: roadmap has per-tenant policies in 'Private' first, then Dedicated. Global heuristics remain default for hosted.
taylor: Main tradeoff is memory fragmentation vs isolation. We propose a 2-stage rollout: per-tenant soft-TTL + comptroller that enforces a hard cap if memory pressure spikes.
alex: To add: soft-TTL means entries become low-priority, not immediately evicted. We can keep hot KV shards pinned for 100ms extra to reduce tail latency.
rami: Second: adaptive batching — how are you measuring tail latency during dynamic batching? Are we using p99, p99.9, or a different signal?
maya: We used p99.5 during the demo, but ops wants p99.9 for SLO decisions. Do we have telemetry for p99.9 across batch sizes and seq lengths?
taylor: Yes — console will show p50/p90/p99/p99.9 histograms by route + model. There's also an experimental 'batch latency curve' graph for 10/25/50/100 token seq.
zach: Implementation detail — we sample end-to-end latency on a subset of requests, tag them with batch_size, seq_len, model and stream to the metrics pipeline.
sre-bot: [alert] Note: collecting per-request KV metadata increases cardinality. We throttle sampling to 2% by default.
maya: Third: kernel selection. Can customers pin a specific kernel or compiled variant per-model in Dedicated? And will that be supported in Private?
taylor: Customers on Dedicated will be able to pin 'kernel_profile' in the model manifest (alpha next month). Private will follow with an operator-managed mapping.
taylor: We also expose a compatibility check API so the control plane can validate pinned kernels won't break fallback chains.
alex: Related: we're adding a safe-fallback sequence: pinned -> compatible-quantized -> generic. Op teams can reorder policy for critical tenants.
rami: On rollout: what's the plan if a kernel change causes a tiny perf regression but big cost win? Manual canary + automatic rollback?
maya: Leadership asked for a policy: auto-rollback only for regressions that exceed both latency SLO delta and error-rate delta. Cost improvements alone won't trigger rollback.
zach: Ops note: we'll enable canary windows per pool and run a quick load test (10k ops) during rollout to catch micro-regressions.
maya: Quick config example requested by a customer — can we show the manifest snippet for pinning a kernel?
taylor: Sure — example below (alpha syntax):

```
model_manifest:
  model_name: "redwood-7b"
  kernel_profile: "nvfuser-v3"
  kernel_policy:
    fallback: ["quantized-8bit", "generic-cuda"]
    allow_autotune: false
```

maya: Last thing: are there any changes to the prewarm strategy for bursty workloads? We had questions about cold starts with large KV warmups.
alex: Yes — new prewarm will warm KV prefixes opportunistically and snapshot hot KV to disk between bursts. That reduces cold penalty by ~35% in our tests.
rami: Ops will expose a per-route 'prewarm_budget' so customers can pay to keep X persistent workers warmed.
maya: Awesome. Thanks — can we get follow-up doc / RFC so the customer-facing team can answer enterprise questions?
taylor: Will publish RFC + migration plan by next Wednesday. I'll drop the link here when ready.
maya: :thumbsup: thanks all.
